title: Sonic onramp and KV 'spark' seeder: staged, workload-aware weight onboarding for Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: cold-start tail latency and bursty onboarding costs for Dedicated customers remain a primary friction point. Current warm-pool approaches load full weight snapshots and bulk-fill KV which causes long startup spikes and unpredictable throughput during the first N minutes after tenant attach. This ticket proposes 'Sonic onramp' — a lightweight, incremental weight-onboarding pipeline plus a KV 'spark' seeder that reduces cold-start amplification while preserving throughput guarantees and tenant isolation.

Proposal summary: implement a three-phase admission and prewarm pipeline for Dedicated nodes: (1) signature-only admission: admit new tenant to a light sandbox and serve short low-cost warmup traces; (2) staged weight streaming: load essential attention + embedding slices first, then progressively expand residency based on real request profile; (3) KV spark seeding: seed likely KV prefixes using a probabilistic hotset sampler derived from historical traces and short synthetic probes. Admission control will enforce per-tenant throughput floors and a soft-start multiplier that ramps request tokens/sec to the committed throughput to avoid saturating background fetch I/O.

Goals and success metrics: reduce 95th pct cold-start latency from X to <= 30% of baseline; reduce early-phase token cost by >= 40%; meet per-tenant throughput guarantee within 90s for 95% of onboarding events; no regression in steady-state throughput/latency.

Design decisions and trade-offs: choose progressive weight residency instead of eager full snapshot to lower peak I/O and memory pressure; use probabilistic KV seeding so we avoid full prefix enumeration which is costly for large token maps; implement tenant soft-throttles to trade slightly longer ramp for stable cluster behavior. We prefer deterministic probes over blind prefetch for regulated tenants (configurable).

API/Config surface: new dedicated config block: "onramp.strategy" = [fast, staged, deterministic]; "onramp.soft_start_seconds" integer; "kv.seeder.mode" = [spark, full, disabled]; per-tenant policy can pin strategy and throughput-floor. Backwards compatible defaults mimic current warm-pool behavior.

Observability and validation: instrument onboarding lifecycle phases with events (admit, seed_start, weight_slice_load, seed_end, ramp_complete). Expose time-to-throughput, early-token-cost, and KV-hit-rates in Console. Add a rollout dashboard and a smoke job that simulates tenant attach patterns.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated on Dedicated fleets; start with internal alpha (infra team), then a small subset of low-risk tenants (opt-in), then gradual ramp with automatic rollback if early-token-cost or 95th-latency cross thresholds.

Risks and mitigations: incorrect hotset estimates can hurt quality — mitigate with a conservative default and a periodic small probe policy to validate seeds; IO bursts during staged loads — mitigate with scheduler backpressure + background throttling and kernel I/O reservations.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Sonic+Onramp+Design, proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7682, benchmark harness: https://bench.redwood.dev/sonic-onramp-alpha

Next steps: complete proto PR reviews, add KV seeder sampler to pipeline, implement per-tenant soft throttles, and create console metrics and alerts.
